title: Resolving the isospin-mixing anomaly in $^{26}$Si from $^{26}$P $β$-decay
byline: Johansson; B S O; Jensen; E A M; Nielsen; J S; Adams; Borge; M J G; Dopfer; Fynbo; H O U; Jonson; Kristensen; M V; Madurga; E D; Riisager; Sumithrarachchi; C S;
html:
Abstract:The $\beta$-delayed one- and two-proton emission of the proton-dripline nucleus $^{26}$P provides a sensitive probe of isospin symmetry-breaking. A recent study reported the observation of a strongly isospin-mixed doublet in $^{26}$Si, comprised of the $T = 2$ Isobaric Analog State (IAS) and a state at 13380 keV, yielding a record-high isospin mixing matrix element. We report a new high-resolution measurement of the $^{26}$P $\beta$-delayed charged-particle decay performed at the Facility for Rare Isotope Beams (FRIB), shedding new light on the isospin mixing in this decay. By utilizing low-energy beam implantation from the Advanced Cryogenic Gas Stopper (ACGS), we obtained clean one-proton and two-proton decay spectra. Our high statistics study show discrepancies in decay branches and the existence of a 13380 keV state in $^{26}$Si is unsupported by our data. Our deduced branching ratio to the IAS is fully consistent with the expectation from the Fermi sum rule. Consequently, the claim of strong isospin mixing in $^{26}$Si is refuted, reinstating standard theoretical expectations for isospin mixing in nuclei.
